newsitem.title: USA: Heart of U.S. Midwest still seen dry this weekend.
newsitem.headline: Heart of U.S. Midwest still seen dry this weekend.

text.p: Most of the central U.S. Midwest is expected to stay dry through the weekend and no significant precipitation is seen until the middle of next week, U.S. meteorologists said.

"Although there will be some showers around, we don't expect any general, significant shower activity in the heart of the Corn Belt until the mid to late part of next week," said David Taylor, with Weather Services Corp in Lexington, Mass.
Showers are expected in the upper Great Lakes, northern Minnesota and Wisconsin today and tonight but rainfall totals are expected to be light, Taylor said.
Rainfall totals this weekend are seen near 0.01 to 0.40 of an inch across the extreme northern portions of the Corn Belt, Taylor said.

Fred Gesser, meteorolgist with Weather Express Inc in Omaha, Neb. sees a system bringing rainfall ranging from 0.25 to 1.50 inch with 30 to 40 percent coverage in parts of Iowa, Nebraska, southern Minnesota, northwestern Illinois and southern Wisconsin on Friday and Saturday.
"We'll see similar amounts of coverage for eastern Indiana, southern Michigan and Ohio on Sunday and into Monday," Gesser said.
Gesser said the next significant chance of rain would come on August 8 or 9 from a cold front system moving west to east.
"It's weak, though, and not very good looking," Gesser said.
